Get in touch with Karl

Karl is originally from Dublin. He trained at the British School of Osteopathy in London, completing his four-year honours degree in 1995. In 1996, he opened his own clinic in Galway.

After many years in practice, he still enjoys working with people of different ages and the variety of problems they bring. He takes time to explain his approach and offer practical advice.

OSTEOPATHY

What is osteopathy?

Osteopathy is a hands-on approach to care for muscles, joints and tendons.

Karl starts by listening to your problem and looking at your movement and posture. Depending on the assessment, treatment may include gentle stretching and muscle work, alongside advice and exercises to try yourself.

The approach is guided by your assessment. If a concern needs another professional’s input, Karl may refer you to your GP or a specialist.

Explore your consultation

YOUR CONSULTATION

What to expect.

Approximately one hour to talk through your problem, assess your movement and discuss care and practical advice.

01

Talk

Talk through your problem, how it started and how it affects everyday life.

02

Assess

Karl looks at your movement and posture to help decide what may be appropriate.

03

Treat

Gentle stretches and muscle work. Joint release may be considered when safe and useful.

04

Move forward

Discuss stretches, exercises and returning to everyday movement and sport.

THE APPROACH

Understand your problem.
Take an active part in your care.

The aim is to support a return to movement with practical advice and self-management, without encouraging unnecessary long-term dependence on treatment.

AWAY FROM THE CLINIC

A personal interest
in movement.

Karl has a genuine personal interest in movement and sport. He skis, surfs and does archery, and enjoys running and triathlon.

He completed the Ironman Triathlon in Copenhagen in 2014, six half-Ironman races and four marathons, including Dublin and Dingle.

Part of his personal background, alongside his work as an osteopath.

What is osteopathy?

A hands-on approach to care for muscles, joints and tendons. Karl considers your history, movement and posture when discussing treatment and advice.

What happens during a first consultation?

Karl listens to the history of your problem and assesses your movement and posture. Treatment may include gentle stretches and muscle work, with joint release considered when safe and useful. He also gives advice on self-help stretches and exercises. The approach depends on your assessment.

How long does a consultation take?

A first consultation lasts approximately one hour, including assessment, treatment and advice on self-help stretches.

What does a first consultation cost?

A first consultation costs €75.

What does a follow-up cost?

A follow-up consultation costs €70.

What are the opening hours?

Monday to Thursday: 9:15am — first appointment; 5:30pm — last appointment. Friday: 9:15am — 11:45am. View opening hours.

What should I wear?

See the Before you visit guidance for what to wear.

6 Monksfield, Salthill, Galway, H91 XN61, Ireland. The entrance is at the back of the house, down the slope. Parking is available in the driveway. Find the clinic.
